newsitem.title: USA: Top Florida lawmaker wins Democratic House primary.
newsitem.headline: Top Florida lawmaker wins Democratic House primary.

text.p: Florida House Majority Leader Jim Davis Tuesday defeated former Tampa Mayor Sandy Freedman in a runoff election to choose the Democrat who will run for the U.S. House seat being vacated by retiring 17-term Democratic Congressman Sam Gibbons.
Gibbons' 11th District House seat was seen as the most vulnerable to Republic takeover of the three open House seats in Florida.

Although she had been considered the front-runner up until election night, Freedman, 52, conceded the race to Davis, 38, when, with 80 percent of the returns in, Davis led with 58 percent of the vote to her 42 percent.
Freedman called Davis to congratulate him and asked her supporters to work for him in the Nov. 5 contest against Republican Mark Sharpe, 36.

Sharpe, a private school teacher, was nominated without opposition. He ran against Gibbons in 1992 and 1994, losing both times, but coming near an upset in 1994. Sharpe's previous campaigns, based on balancing the federal budget, have made him familiar to voters.
Gibbons, who represented Tampa for 17 terms, is retiring at the end of the current term.
